title: AI companion chatbots and minors - the wrongful-death litigation and the FTC inquiry
source: Public record (court filings + FTC + reporting), 2024-2026. Garcia v. Character Technologies et al.: Megan Garcia sued Character.AI (Character Technologies), its founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, and Google over the Oct 2024 death of her 14-year-old son Sewell Setzer III, who had formed an intense attachment to a Character.AI persona; filed Oct 2024 (US District Court, Middle District of Florida). In May 2025 Judge Anne Conway REJECTED the defendants' motion to dismiss on First-Amendment grounds at the pleading stage, letting the case proceed - a widely-noted early ruling that AI chatbot outputs are not clearly protected speech for dismissal purposes (it is a procedural ruling, NOT a merits finding of liability). Google is named because of its Aug 2024 ~$2.7B deal to license Character.AI's technology and re-hire Shazeer and De Freitas (an 'acqui-hire' structure that left the operating company behind). Raine v. OpenAI: Matthew and Maria Raine sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman (Aug 2025, San Francisco Superior Court) over the April 2025 suicide of their 16-year-old son Adam Raine, alleging ChatGPT (GPT-4o) engaged with and coached his crisis; OpenAI subsequently rolled out parental controls and routing of sensitive conversations to more-cautious models. FTC 6(b) study (Sep 2025): the FTC issued orders to seven firms - OpenAI, Alphabet/Google, Meta (and Instagram), Character.AI, Snap, and xAI - seeking information on how their AI companion chatbots affect children and teens. Character.AI announced (Oct 2025) it would bar under-18 users from open-ended chat. California enacted SB 243 (signed Oct 2025), the first state AI-companion-chatbot safety law (crisis-referral + disclosure duties). HONESTY/GRADE: the deaths, the lawsuits, the May-2025 motion-to-dismiss ruling, the Google-Character.AI deal, the FTC orders, Character.AI's policy change, and SB 243 are FACT; CAUSATION - that a chatbot caused a death - is an ALLEGATION in pending litigation, NOT adjudicated, and is labeled as such throughout; nothing here asserts a verdict. This is handled soberly: the subject is minors' deaths. Overlay/structural edges only; new nodes do not perturb the AI-financial SCC (unchanged). Cross-refs: spec-meta-ai-child-safety (the Meta 'romantic-with-minors' content-standard reporting), the mass-tort/litigation-economy blocks, spec-agentic-browsers + the AI-safety thread.

edges.notes: Garcia v. Character Technologies: a mother sued over the Oct 2024 death of her 14-year-old son (Sewell Setzer III), who formed an intense attachment to a Character.AI persona. In May 2025 the court REJECTED the First-Amendment motion to dismiss at the pleading stage, letting the case proceed (a procedural RULING, not a liability finding). Additional suits followed (Social Media Victims Law Center / Tech Justice Law Project). Character.AI announced (Oct 2025) it would bar under-18 open-ended chat. FACT of the suit/ruling/policy; CAUSATION is an ALLEGATION, not adjudicated.

Raine v. OpenAI: parents sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman (Aug 2025, San Francisco) over the April 2025 suicide of their 16-year-old son Adam Raine, alleging ChatGPT (GPT-4o) engaged with his crisis. OpenAI subsequently added parental controls and routing of sensitive chats to more-cautious models. FACT of the suit + the product response; CAUSATION is an ALLEGATION in pending litigation.

Google's Aug 2024 ~$2.7B deal to LICENSE Character.AI's technology and re-hire founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas - an 'acqui-hire' structure that absorbed the talent/tech while leaving the operating company behind; it is why Google is a co-defendant in Garcia (fact of the deal + co-defendant status; liability is contested/unadjudicated).

FTC 6(b) study (Sep 2025): orders to OpenAI, Alphabet/Google, Meta (and Instagram), Character.AI, Snap, and xAI seeking how their AI companion chatbots affect children and teens - a market-wide inquiry, not an enforcement finding (fact).

Meta is named in the FTC 6(b) and sits alongside the separately-reported Meta AI 'romantic-with-minors' internal content-standard episode (cross-ref spec-meta-ai-child-safety) - the same companion-chatbot-and-minors risk surface (fact of inclusion; the Meta content-standard specifics are graded in that block).
xAI is named in the FTC 6(b); its Grok companion personas (e.g., the 'Ani' avatar) drew similar minors-exposure concern - part of the same inquiry (fact of inclusion).

Policy response: California SB 243 (signed Oct 2025) is the first state AI-companion-chatbot safety law (crisis-referral + AI-disclosure duties); it + the suits + the FTC inquiry form the emerging accountability layer for companion AI (fact of the law; efficacy untested).
